title: Medical Bill Audit
tagline: Upload an itemized hospital bill and see every line checked against that hospital's own posted prices
problem: US patients routinely receive hospital bills with duplicate charges, upcoded visits and items never delivered, and the error rate is often put far higher than people expect (industry figures vary widely, est.). Most patients never request an itemized bill or know what a CPT code means. Billing offices rarely volunteer corrections, so overcharges of hundreds to thousands of dollars go unchallenged.
solution: Upload your itemized hospital bill and get instant AI analysis identifying errors, duplicate charges, upcoding, and unbundled services. The system compares charges against Medicare reimbursement rates and regional pricing benchmarks, flags statistical anomalies, and generates professional dispute letters with specific billing codes and legal references. Users have reported average savings of $1,200 per audited bill.
target_audience: Patients with bills over $1000; uninsured/underinsured; medical debt collectors
pricing: Free bill scan; $49 per full audit with dispute letter, or 20% of verified savings over $200 (capped at $500)
competitors: Goodbill; Counterforce Health; Resolve Medical Bills; general AI assistants (ChatGPT/Claude)
competitor_gap: Free tools write letters but do not benchmark each line against that hospital's own posted negotiated rates or track which arguments a given billing office accepts
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): My hospital bill has errors I cant understand | I got charged for services I never received | I cant afford this medical bill what do I do
unique_data_capture: Line-item corpus of itemized hospital bills (CPT/HCPCS/revenue codes) matched to each hospital's published price-transparency negotiated rates, plus which disputes each billing office reversed and how fast
commoditization_risk: High: consumers already paste bills into general AI assistants, Counterforce Health is free for insurance appeals, and employer-side vendors like Goodbill sell bill advocacy to plans
regulatory_notes: HIPAA does not apply to a consumer-directed app but FTC Health Breach Notification Rule does; avoid implying legal representation; success fees on medical debt need clear disclosure
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible as SaaS; needs a reliable price-transparency data pipeline and careful privacy handling
mvp_features: Bill OCR and parsing, error detection engine, Medicare rate comparison, dispute letter generator, savings calculator
review_notes: Biggest risk is that a free general AI assistant gives 80% of the value; the moat has to come from hospital-specific rate and outcome data
score_justification: L4 LLM+OCR reads itemized bills and codes; E4 OCR+rules MVP in weeks; A4 steady 'hospital bill error' searches; P2 no built-in channel, SEO only; M3 dispute-outcome data by hospital; W3 patients pay but free AI and nonprofits undercut

title: Insurance Claim Max
tagline: Never leave money on the table - AI coach for insurance claims that knows what adjusters know
problem: Homeowners and drivers filing property or auto claims face adjusters who handle hundreds of claims a year and know exactly which policy provisions to lean on. Most policyholders never read their policy, accept the first offer and miss covered items such as code upgrades or loss of use. Public adjusters help but take 10-20% of the payout and avoid small claims.
solution: Get the same intelligence insurance adjusters use -- but working for you. Upload your policy and claim details, and the AI instantly identifies coverage you're entitled to, calculates fair settlement ranges using actual claims data, and coaches you through every step of negotiation. Generates documentation checklists, counter-offer letters, and escalation strategies that mirror what public adjusters charge thousands for.
target_audience: Homeowners with property damage; auto accident claimants; anyone denied or lowballed
competitors: Licensed public adjusters; Claim Doctor and similar claim-help services; general AI assistants
competitor_gap: Public adjusters are expensive and skip small claims; generic AI cannot say what a fair payout looks like for a given insurer and loss type
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): My claim was denied unfairly
unique_data_capture: Settlement offers vs final payouts by insurer, claim type, state and adjuster tactic, captured from users' uploaded claim letters over time
commoditization_risk: Medium: general AI assistants can explain a policy, but they lack insurer-specific settlement history
regulatory_notes: Negotiating a claim for a fee can require a public adjuster license in most states; stay strictly in coaching/self-help mode and avoid UPL in disputed bad-faith claims
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible as a self-help SaaS; scaling into representation needs licensed adjuster partners
mvp_features: Policy analyzer + claim value estimator + documentation checklist + appeal letter generator
review_notes: Must stay on the coaching side of public-adjuster licensing laws or partner with licensed adjusters
score_justification: L4 AI reads policy and maps coverage; E4 document Q&A MVP fast; A3 spikes after disasters; P2 no native channel; M3 settlement-by-insurer data; W4 public adjusters take 10-20% so buyers pay

title: Contractor Bid Check
tagline: Know if youre getting ripped off before you sign - AI analysis of home improvement quotes
problem: Homeowners planning a $5K-$50K renovation usually collect two or three quotes they cannot really compare: line items differ, scope is vague and material grades are unstated. Low bids often hide change orders and high bids exploit uncertainty, so people pick on gut feel. Free cost guides give national averages, not a read of the actual quote on the table.
solution: Snap a photo of any home improvement quote and get an instant breakdown showing whether materials, labor, and margins are in line with local market rates. The AI flags missing scope items that often become expensive change orders, identifies suspiciously low bids that signal corner-cutting, and highlights line items where you're being overcharged. Includes a side-by-side comparison tool for evaluating multiple bids and generates informed questions to ask each contractor.
target_audience: Homeowners planning renovations $5K+; property investors; home flippers
competitors: Angi/HomeAdvisor cost guides; Fixr cost guides; general AI assistants; asking for more bids
competitor_gap: Cost guides are national averages and do not read your actual quote or flag missing scope items; no one aggregates real quotes by zip
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Is my contractor quote too high | How to compare home renovation bids | Contractor added change orders I didn't approve
unique_data_capture: Structured database of real contractor quotes by trade, zip code, scope and material grade, with later outcomes (change orders, final cost) reported by users
commoditization_risk: Medium: a general AI assistant can read a quote, but without local quote benchmarks it can only guess at fair prices
regulatory_notes: None notable beyond avoiding defamatory claims about named contractors; present ranges as estimates
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible; the hard part is seeding the quote database (scrape public bid data, partner with home inspectors and reno communities)
mvp_features: Quote OCR and parsing, local rate database, scope gap detector, bid comparison tool, question generator for contractor interviews
review_notes: Cold-start of the quote database is the open question; without enough local quotes, benchmarks fall back to the same averages as free cost guides
score_justification: L4 AI parses quote photos into line items; E4 OCR+LLM+cost tables in weeks; A4 'is this quote fair' is a constant homeowner question; P3 Nextdoor/Reddit/home-reno groups and SEO; M5 every quote adds trade/region price data; W4 homeowners spending $5K+ will pay $19 to check

title: Vet Bill Audit
tagline: Love your pet but not the bill - AI that spots unnecessary vet charges and finds alternatives
target_segment: Pet owners facing expensive vet bills
problem: Pet owners facing a dental cleaning, surgery or emergency visit often see estimates that vary several-fold between clinics in the same city, with little explanation. Bills arrive in a stressful moment, and owners rarely know which diagnostics are optional or what a fair local price is. Vet pricing is not posted, so there is no easy way to compare.
solution: Upload your vet bill or estimate and get a transparent breakdown comparing charges against regional veterinary pricing data. The AI identifies potentially unnecessary tests and procedures, suggests lower-cost alternatives like compounding pharmacies and veterinary schools, and flags when a second opinion could save hundreds. Includes a chronic condition cost planner that helps pet owners budget for ongoing care without sacrificing quality.
target_audience: Pet owners facing expensive vet bills; those with chronic pet conditions; multi-pet households
competitors: DIR-002 Vet Price Compare (corpus); Pawlicy Advisor; general AI assistants; vet school clinics
competitor_gap: No one turns individual invoices into clinic-level price transparency for owners
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): My vet bill is way too expensive | Are these vet tests really necessary | How to find affordable vet care for my dog
unique_data_capture: Itemized vet invoices and estimates by clinic, zip, species and procedure, giving real local price ranges for common treatments
commoditization_risk: Medium: general AI can explain a vet bill, but clinic-level price comparisons need crowdsourced invoices
regulatory_notes: Must not second-guess clinical necessity in a way that amounts to veterinary advice; frame as price comparison and questions to ask
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible; needs a data-seeding plan (invoice uploads from pet communities)
mvp_features: Bill OCR and parsing, regional vet price database, unnecessary test detector, alternative provider finder, chronic care cost planner
review_notes: Overlaps corpus idea DIR-002 Vet Price Compare; merge the two or keep only the invoice-audit angle
score_justification: L4 AI reads invoices and maps procedure codes; E4 OCR MVP fast; A4 vet-cost complaints are common; P2 SEO/pet groups only; M4 clinic-level price data compounds; W3 owners pay emotionally but few pay for audits

title: Salary Negotiator
tagline: Companies have the playbook - now you do too. AI salary negotiation coach with real data
target_segment: Job seekers with offers in hand
problem: Many candidates accept the first job offer without negotiating, even though recruiters often expect a counter and have room within a salary band. Candidates usually lack data on what peers at the same company and level earn, and fear losing the offer. Leaving 5-10% on the table at the start compounds through every later raise.
solution: Paste your job offer and the AI instantly analyzes it against real compensation data for your role, level, location, and company size. Identifies where the offer falls versus market (base, equity, bonus, benefits), generates word-for-word negotiation scripts for phone and email, and coaches you through counter-offer strategy. Includes live practice mode where the AI role-plays as the hiring manager so you can rehearse before the real conversation.
target_audience: Job seekers with offers in hand; career changers; new graduates entering the workforce
pricing: $49 per offer analysis or $19/mo for job search period
competitors: Levels.fyi negotiation coaching; Glassdoor; Payscale; general AI assistants
competitor_gap: Cheap self-serve tier between free AI scripts and $1,250 human coaching, for non-tech roles Levels.fyi does not cover
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): How to negotiate salary for new job | Is my job offer competitive | What to say when negotiating a raise
unique_data_capture: Verified offer letters and counter-offer outcomes by company, level, location and negotiation script used
commoditization_risk: High: general AI assistants role-play negotiations well and Levels.fyi offers both free data and paid coaching
regulatory_notes: None notable; handle offer letters as confidential employee data
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible; the hard part is getting real offer data outside big tech
mvp_features: Offer analyzer + market comp + negotiation script generator + counter offer calculator
review_notes: Squeezed between free AI role-play and Levels.fyi's guaranteed-outcome coaching; later corpus idea CLAUDE-126 Salary Data Decoder overlaps
score_justification: L3 AI scripts and role-play; E4 fast; A4 strong 'how to negotiate salary' demand; P2 LinkedIn/SEO only; M3 offer-and-outcome data; W4 Levels.fyi coaching sells at $1,250+

title: Debt Settlement Coach
tagline: Creditors have playbooks - now you do too. AI guide to settling debt for less
target_segment: Consumers with credit card debt in collections
problem: Consumers with charged-off credit cards, medical debt or accounts in collections often do not know creditors and debt buyers regularly settle for a fraction of the balance. Debt-settlement companies charge 15-25% of enrolled debt and take years, while people negotiating alone say the wrong things or pay without written terms. Mistakes can restart collection or create tax surprises.
solution: Enter your debt details -- type, amount, age, and creditor -- and get an instant analysis of settlement likelihood based on patterns from thousands of resolved cases. The AI tells you exactly when to negotiate (debt age matters enormously), what percentage to offer first, what to say and never say to collectors, and how to document everything to prevent future disputes. Generates settlement offer letters and paid-in-full confirmation templates that protect you legally.
target_audience: Consumers with credit card debt in collections; people with medical debt; borrowers considering debt-settlement firms
competitors: National Debt Relief and other settlement firms; nonprofit credit counseling (NFCC); general AI assistants
competitor_gap: Settlement firms charge 15-25% and take years; nonprofits push repayment plans; no cheap self-serve tool with creditor-specific odds
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): How to settle debt for less than I owe | What to say to debt collectors | Can I negotiate my credit card debt down
unique_data_capture: Accepted settlement percentages by creditor or debt buyer, debt age and balance, with time-to-settle and paperwork outcomes
commoditization_risk: Medium: general AI can draft letters, but creditor-specific settlement odds require outcome data
regulatory_notes: Debt-relief services face the FTC Telemarketing Sales Rule advance-fee ban and state debt-adjuster licensing; FDCPA and tax on forgiven debt must be explained; avoid acting as a debt-settlement company
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible as self-help software; must check state debt-adjuster laws before charging
mvp_features: Debt analyzer + settlement calculator + script generator + documentation templates
review_notes: Regulatory exposure: some states treat paid debt-settlement help as a licensed activity
score_justification: L4 AI drafts offers and scripts; E4 fast; A4 large indebted audience; P2 SEO and debt forums; M3 settlement % by creditor; W3 distressed users have little cash

title: Property Tax Appeal
tagline: Your home is overassessed - AI that finds the proof and writes the appeal
problem: Assessed values often lag or overshoot the market, and many homeowners never appeal even though informal reviews and boards of review regularly reduce assessments. The process differs by county, deadlines are short and finding comparable sales takes hours. An unchallenged over-assessment costs money every year until it is fixed.
solution: Enter your property address and the AI pulls your current assessment, finds comparable properties that sold for less, identifies assessment errors, and calculates your potential annual savings. Generates a complete appeal package including comparable sales analysis, photos documentation guide, and jurisdiction-specific appeal forms pre-filled with your information. Guides you through hearing preparation with what to say and what evidence boards actually care about.
target_audience: Homeowners in any state; property investors; tax consultants
pricing: Free analysis / $99 or 25% of first year savings
competitors: Ownwell; local property tax consultants; county self-help portals
competitor_gap: Incumbents focus on high-population states; many counties remain unserved
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): My property tax assessment is too high | How to appeal property tax assessment | Property taxes went up way too much this year
unique_data_capture: Appeal filings and board decisions by county, property type and argument, linked to assessed vs sale values
commoditization_risk: Medium: Ownwell and local tax consultants already run success-fee appeals; general AI can draft a letter but cannot pull comps
regulatory_notes: Some states license property-tax consultants (e.g. Texas); representation at hearings may require registration
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible county by county; data acquisition per county is the bottleneck
mvp_features: Assessment lookup + comp finder + error detection + appeal letter generator
review_notes: Heavy competition from Ownwell in big states; profitability depends on picking under-served counties
score_justification: L4 AI comp selection and appeal drafting; E3 needs county assessor data per jurisdiction; A4 high seasonal demand; P2 SEO/direct mail; M4 appeal outcomes by county; W4 Ownwell-style success fees work

title: Influencer Rate Card
tagline: Brands have budgets - now you know them. AI that helps creators price brand deals correctly
problem: Micro and mid-size creators are often unsure what to charge for a sponsored post, video or bundle, so they accept a brand's first offer. Brands and agencies see many deals and know their budgets, while creators rely on rough follower-count formulas. Underpricing early deals anchors future rates low.
solution: Connect your social profiles and the AI calculates your true market value using engagement rates, audience demographics, niche CPM benchmarks, and brand deal databases. Generates a professional rate card, media kit, and pitch templates that position you at your actual worth -- not the lowball figure brands open with. Includes counter-offer scripts for when brands push back and a deal tracker to benchmark your rates over time.
target_audience: Content creators with 1K-500K followers; micro-influencers undercharging for posts; YouTubers and TikTokers negotiating brand deals
competitors: Collabstr; Passionfroot; Beacons media kits; free influencer rate calculators
competitor_gap: Calculators use follower-count formulas, not real closed-deal prices
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): How much should I charge for a sponsored post | Brand offered me a deal is this rate fair | How to make a media kit as an influencer
unique_data_capture: Closed brand-deal prices by platform, niche, follower band, engagement rate and deliverable type, submitted by creators
commoditization_risk: Medium: creator marketplaces and media-kit tools include free rate calculators
regulatory_notes: FTC endorsement disclosure guidance should be built into deal templates
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible
mvp_features: Metric analyzer + rate calculator + pitch generator + negotiation scripts
review_notes: Crowded creator-tools market; corpus DIR-034 Content Creator Rates and CLAUDE-185 overlap
score_justification: L4 AI computes rates from engagement; E4 social API MVP; A4 creators ask constantly; P2 creator communities but no store; M3 deal data; W3 small creators are price-sensitive

unique_data_capture: Line-item vendor pricing (unit price, term, discount, renewal uplift) across SMB invoices by category and company size

title: Franchise Due Diligence
tagline: Franchisors have sales teams - you have this. AI that analyzes FDD documents for red flags
problem: Prospective franchise buyers receive a 200+ page Franchise Disclosure Document and often have 14 days before signing. Earnings claims in Item 19 are optional and hard to compare, while closure and transfer counts in Item 20 are buried in tables. Brokers are usually paid by franchisors, so buyers investing their savings get little independent analysis.
solution: Upload your Franchise Disclosure Document and the AI analyzes all 23 required items, focusing on the financial representations in Item 19, litigation history in Item 3, and franchisee turnover in Items 20-21. Flags earnings claims that don't match reality, identifies concerning patterns in franchisee lawsuits, and calculates true total investment including hidden costs. Generates a due diligence report with specific questions to ask existing franchisees and red flags to walk away from.
target_audience: Prospective franchise buyers; franchise consultants; franchise attorneys doing initial screening
competitors: FRANdata (B2B lenders/franchisors); franchise attorneys; franchise brokers (paid by franchisors); general AI assistants
competitor_gap: FRANdata sells to lenders and franchisors, not buyers; brokers are paid by franchisors; no affordable buyer-side benchmark tool
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Is this franchise opportunity legit | How to read a franchise disclosure document | Franchise didn't make the money they promised
unique_data_capture: Normalized database of FDDs across years and brands: Item 19 earnings claims, Item 20 openings/closures/transfers, Item 3 litigation and Item 7 investment ranges, giving brand-vs-category benchmarks
commoditization_risk: Medium: a general AI assistant can summarize one FDD, but year-over-year, cross-brand benchmarks need a curated database
regulatory_notes: Present as due-diligence analysis, not legal advice; recommend franchise attorney review before signing; FDDs are public records in registration states
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible; FDDs can be collected from state registration databases
mvp_features: FDD parser, Item 19 financial analyzer, litigation pattern detector, true cost calculator, franchisee question generator, red flag report
review_notes: Main risk is the small buyer pool; upsell to franchise attorneys and SBA lenders may be needed
score_justification: L4 AI extracts all 23 FDD Items; E4 PDF parsing + LLM, weeks; A3 focused but high-intent buyer niche; P3 franchise expos, Reddit r/franchise, SEO on brand names; M4 cross-brand Item 19/20 benchmarks compound; W5 buyers investing $100K-$1M+ already pay attorneys $2-5K

title: Commercial Lease Review
tagline: Commercial landlords have attorneys - small businesses dont. AI that levels the playing field
problem: Small business owners signing a first commercial lease face terms built by landlords' attorneys: uncapped CAM charges, personal guarantees, relocation clauses and weak renewal options. Unlike residential leases, almost everything is negotiable, but most owners do not know market norms. A bad lease can sink a restaurant or shop before it becomes profitable.
solution: Upload your commercial lease or term sheet and the AI identifies every clause that sophisticated landlords use to extract extra money -- hidden CAM charges, personal guarantee traps, demolition clauses, restrictive use provisions, and unfavorable renewal terms. Benchmarks your rent and terms against comparable commercial spaces in your market. Generates a redline document with specific counter-proposals and negotiation talking points that show you understand commercial real estate.
target_audience: Small business owners signing leases; restaurant owners; retail entrepreneurs
competitors: Tenant-rep brokers (often free to tenants); commercial real-estate attorneys; general AI assistants
competitor_gap: Tenant-rep brokers focus on larger deals; small tenants get no market benchmarks
demand_evidence: v1 search phrases (unverified): Commercial lease CAM charges too high | Should I sign a personal guarantee for my business lease | How to negotiate commercial lease terms as small business
unique_data_capture: Commercial lease terms (rent/sq ft, CAM caps, guarantees, TI allowances, renewal options) by city, property type and tenant size
commoditization_risk: Medium: general AI can redline a lease; local term benchmarks are the differentiator
regulatory_notes: UPL risk lower for business clients but redlines must be framed as negotiation suggestions; recommend attorney review
founder_feasibility: Solo-feasible
mvp_features: Lease parser + clause analyzer + negotiation generator + market comparison
review_notes: Requires local lease-term data to beat a free AI read
score_justification: L4 AI clause extraction and redlines; E4 fast; A3 moderate; P2 SBA/SBDC channels; M3 lease terms by market; W4 businesses pay $1-3K for attorney review

title: IEP Advocate

competitor_gap: Free resources explain the process; nobody tells a parent what services similar children in their district received
